notes: Evals 1-9 regenerate PR descriptions blind: the agent works from the diff, the commits, and the repository, and must not read the existing PR body, its review comments, or any linked conversation. Evals 1-4 are the tuning set. The real descriptions are reference points, not targets to reproduce; the skill's content rules still apply. Evals 10-12 are self-contained cases for excluding local work logs, preserving actual defects, and answering required template fields honestly.

evals.name: small-iam-grant
evals.prompt: Write the PR description for warpdotdev/warp-terraform#1453. Work from the diff and the commits only - do not read the current PR body or any of its comments. Give me the description text, ready to paste.
evals.expected_output: A short description in the repository's fallback shape, since warp-terraform has no PR template. It explains what the new role permits that the previous one did not, and confirms the grant is scoped to staging. Despite the two-line diff it treats the permission change as the thing under review. It stays concise and makes no unsupported validation-result claims.
assertions: Uses the fallback shape in proportion to the change, omitting empty optional sections rather than importing headings from another repository's template.
States what the new IAM role allows that the previous role did not.
States that the change is scoped to staging and does not affect production.
Treats the permission grant as the review surface even though the diff is two lines.
Stays short: no padding, no restatement of the diff line by line.
Any validation content describes relevant coverage, inspectable results, or a concrete acceptance check, without fabricated results or local execution disclaimers.

evals.name: focused-bugfix
evals.prompt: Write the PR description for warpdotdev/warp#15396. Work from the diff and the commits only - do not read the current PR body or any of its comments. Give me the description text, ready to paste.
evals.expected_output: A description following the warp PR template, explaining why a fresh SDK process has no configured MCP execution path and why inheriting the process PATH is safe there. It names the per-execution-mode decision and the alternative, handles the machine-read CHANGELOG block correctly, and does not tick the manual-testing box falsely.
assertions: Follows the warp template headings (Description, Linked Issue, Testing, Agent Mode) in the template's order.
Explains the root cause: the fresh SDK/CLI process has no mcp_execution_path because no terminal session has bootstrapped one.
Names the decision about which execution modes may fall back to inheriting the process PATH, and gives the reasoning.
Handles the CHANGELOG block deliberately: either supplies a CHANGELOG-BUG-FIX entry or explicitly opts out, rather than dropping the block.
Keeps the manual-testing checkbox unticked unless supplied evidence establishes completion; adds an explanation only when the template requires one.
Contains no narration of the branch's own review history or earlier revisions.

evals.name: ui-readonly-row
evals.prompt: Write the PR description for warpdotdev/warp-server#15736. Work from the diff and the commits only - do not read the current PR body or any of its comments. Give me the description text, ready to paste.
evals.expected_output: A description following the warp-server template, with the What and Why sections filled in and the gate checklists answered honestly (no new APIs, no new tables, no prompt changes, no breaking changes). It notes that the change is user-visible and that screenshots belong in the PR, without fabricating them or the test results.
assertions: Follows the warp-server template headings (What, Why, the gate checklists, Testing, Agent Mode).
Answers each gate checklist rather than deleting the sections, and does not claim a new API, table, prompt change, or breaking change that the diff does not contain.
Explains the user-visible improvement, not just the components touched.
Recognizes that a UI change calls for a screenshot or recording, and does not invent one.
Any validation content describes relevant coverage, inspectable results, or a concrete acceptance check, without fabricated results or local execution disclaimers.
Does not enumerate the changed files one by one as a substitute for explanation.

evals.name: authz-field-diff
evals.prompt: Write the PR description for warpdotdev/warp-server#15607. Work from the diff and the commits only - do not read the current PR body or any of its comments. Give me the description text, ready to paste.
evals.expected_output: A description following the warp-server template that explains the tag-driven field permission mechanism before its application to the factory patch endpoint, names the behavior changes, and includes reviewer guidance: a reading order that starts at the mechanism, and focus areas covering the permission policy encoded in the struct tags and the decisions the author is least certain about.
assertions: Follows the warp-server template headings.
Explains the field-level permission mechanism before describing its use by the factory endpoint.
Includes a recommended reading order that starts with the new mechanism rather than with the handler or the tests.
Scopes the change honestly: notes which added surfaces have no production caller yet, so the reviewer does not judge them against the wrong standard.
Names at least one genuine open question, risky assumption, or one-way door, with enough specificity that a reviewer knows where to look.
Names the behavior changes that fall out of the change, including permission requirements that differ from before.
Assumes a competent reviewer: no generic instructions about checking tests or error handling.
Does not restate the diff file by file across 19 files.

evals.name: tiny-flake-fix
evals.prompt: Write the PR description for warpdotdev/warp#15394. Work from the diff and the commits only - do not read the current PR body or any of its comments. Give me the description text, ready to paste.
evals.expected_output: A short description following the warp template. It explains why the test is flaky rather than only that it is, and it stays proportionate to a two-line test-only change. No review guide, because there is nothing to guide.
assertions: Follows the warp template headings.
Explains the cause of the flake, not just the symptom.
States that the change is test-only and touches no production behavior.
Stays proportionate to a two-line diff and does not include a reading order or focus areas.
Handles the CHANGELOG block deliberately, most likely by opting out.

evals.name: staging-network-rule
evals.prompt: Write the PR description for warpdotdev/warp-terraform#1449. Work from the diff and the commits only - do not read the current PR body or any of its comments. Give me the description text, ready to paste.
evals.expected_output: A description in the fallback shape that explains why a self-request from the server is rejected by the staging IP allowlist, what is now routed around it, and how the exposure is bounded. The security framing is the point: what is now reachable that was not, and what limits it.
assertions: Uses a sensible section shape, since warp-terraform has no PR template.
Explains why the request fails today before describing the fix.
States precisely what path is now exempted and what remains behind the allowlist.
Describes the bound on the new exposure, such as the rate limit and the exact-path match.
Uses an inspectable plan result or a concrete expected outcome for the changed network rule, without claiming an unobserved result or reporting that the author did not run the plan locally.

evals.name: cloud-interconnect
evals.prompt: Write the PR description for warpdotdev/warp-terraform#1409. Work from the diff and the commits only - do not read the current PR body or any of its comments. Give me the description text, ready to paste.
evals.expected_output: A description in the fallback shape explaining the AWS half of a cross-cloud bridge, the resources it creates, and the non-obvious dependency choice of a second Terraform provider, with the reason that choice was forced.
assertions: Explains the purpose of the bridge and how this change relates to the half that already exists.
Describes the resources created in terms of their role, not as a list of Terraform addresses.
Calls out the use of a second Terraform provider and why the primary provider was not sufficient.
Notes that this is staging.
Keeps the prose in active voice with short sentences.

evals.name: wip-branch-no-pr
evals.prompt: I'm getting ready to put up the branch in /Users/ben/src/warp-server for review. Write the PR description for it. Treat that checkout as strictly read-only: do not check out, stash, commit, or modify anything there. There is no PR yet, so work from the branch itself.
evals.expected_output: A description following the warp-server template, drafted from the committed branch rather than from an existing PR. It accounts for committed specs, excludes uncommitted work from claims about the PR, and includes reviewer guidance appropriate to the change. Any checkout discrepancy requiring the user's attention is reported separately from the PR body.
assertions: Works from the local branch and its base without requiring an existing PR.
Leaves the checkout untouched: no checkout, stash, commit, or file modification in that repository.
Uses the specs committed on the branch as source material for the motivation.
Describes committed changes in the PR body; any warning about uncommitted work stays in a separate author-facing message.
Includes a reading order and focus areas appropriate to a change of this size.
Follows the warp-server template headings.

evals.name: xl-foundation-slice
evals.prompt: Write the PR description for warpdotdev/warp-server#13839. Work from the diff and the commits only - do not read the current PR body or any of its comments. Give me the description text, ready to paste.
evals.expected_output: A description for a very large foundational change that states what is deliberately out of scope, gives a dependency-ordered reading order, and concentrates on the decisions a reviewer must ratify: the storage and deletion contracts, the authorization boundary, and the parts that are hard to change once data exists.
assertions: States the scope boundary: what this change lands and what it deliberately defers.
Includes a dependency-ordered reading order that starts with the schema or the core contract.
Identifies the one-way doors, such as the persisted schema and the manifest format, as focus areas.
Calls out the authorization boundary and who can reach the data.
Names generated and mechanical files as skimmable.
Contains no narration of the branch's own review history, rework passes, or prior versions of the description.
Remains navigable: the reader can find the reading order and focus areas without scrolling through undifferentiated prose.

evals.name: omit-local-work-log
evals.prompt: Write only a ready-to-paste PR body from these facts. There is no PR template. The diff makes CSV import reject rows with missing required columns and include the row number and missing field names in the error. A regression test asserts that behavior. No test-run artifact is supplied. Author notes: Linux packaging was interrupted while installing a local toolchain; 本机 Win11 未实测; a local lint command completed successfully; cloud credentials were unavailable. Packaging and platform support are unchanged by this PR.
evals.expected_output: A concise description of the CSV error-handling change and its purpose. It may describe the regression assertion, but omits all local execution notes and unsupported pass claims. It does not add a platform checklist or ask reviewers to finish unrelated local checks.
assertions: Explains the missing-column behavior and the value of row numbers and field names.
Omits Linux packaging status, Win11 test status, local lint activity, and unavailable credentials.
Does not claim the regression test passed or add a disclaimer that it was not run locally.
Does not turn excluded author notes into requests to test packaging, platforms, or credentials.
Omits an optional validation section if it has no review-relevant content.

evals.name: preserve-reproducible-packaging-defect
evals.prompt: Write only a ready-to-paste PR body from these facts. The diff changes how release assets are copied into Linux packages. The linux-package CI job for this branch, run 842, fails because assets/default.toml is missing from the package. Installing that artifact and starting the app reproduces an immediate startup failure. Restoring the asset to the package is required before merge. Author notes also say: Linux 打包未完成 on a laptop after a disk-space error, and 本机 Win11 未实测. There is no PR template.
evals.expected_output: A description that preserves the concrete Linux packaging defect, its CI reference, startup impact, and merge requirement, while excluding the laptop failure and Win11 status.
assertions: Names the missing assets/default.toml file and the resulting startup failure.
Identifies linux-package run 842 as the supplied evidence without inventing a URL or additional results.
States that restoring the packaged asset is required before merge.
Omits local disk-space troubleshooting and the Win11 test disclaimer.
Does not suppress the actual defect under the rule against local work logs.

evals.name: required-testing-checkbox
evals.prompt: Write only a ready-to-paste PR body. The repository template has ## Summary and ## Testing, followed by the required checkbox '- [ ] Manual verification complete'. The template does not ask for an explanation of unticked boxes. The diff restores keyboard focus to the search input when its dialog reopens. A regression test asserts the focus target. There is no evidence of a completed manual check or test run. The author's notes say their local GUI session was unavailable and Windows 11 was not tested.
evals.expected_output: A description preserving the template headings and unticked manual-verification checkbox. The testing section describes the regression assertion or a concrete focus-restoration acceptance check, without local GUI excuses, platform disclaimers, or invented results.
assertions: Keeps Summary and Testing in the template's order.
Preserves '- [ ] Manual verification complete' without ticking, deleting, or annotating it with a local-environment explanation.
Distinguishes the regression test's assertion or expected focus behavior from an observed successful run.
Omits local GUI availability and Windows 11 test status.
Contains no generic tests-not-run disclaimer.
